title: Regional anchoring runway — operator + legal checklist (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight operator-first runway for "anchoring" tenant data to a region (soft and hard anchoring patterns). Goal: give oncall, operators, and Sales Eng a single-page-ish checklist + decision notes to run low-risk migrations and to gather auditable evidence for compliance requests.

Status: WIP. Not the canonical spec. Meant to sit between tabletop notes and the formal runbook.

High-level principles (short):
- Prefer soft anchors (session/edge affinity + evidence capture) before hard-migrating tenant storage.
- Keep audit evidence minimal but rigorous: time-stamped assertion, request headers, operator action id, and digest of stored objects.
- Fall back to safe-readonly mode if anchor enforcement would risk data loss.
- Communicate estimated RTO and potential billing delta to customer before hard moves.

Quick glossary (operator shorthand):
- anchor: the region we intend to tie tenant controls to (not necessarily physical storage toggled yet)
- hard anchor: move/lock tenant storage and KMS to target region
- soft anchor: route traffic, cache affinity, tag telemetry and evidence but keep storage where it is
- pin: tenant-level flag in control-plane that enforces routing (already overloaded term elsewhere)

When to use this runway (trigger list):
- Sales contract requires data residency in EU/UK/APAC and customer requests schedule > 3 business days
- Legal issues: regulatory audit w/ region claim > operator needs to demonstrate evidence
- Operator-detected drift: tenant traffic frequently routed outside contracted region

Operator checklist (pre-flight):
- [ ] Confirm contract/regulatory artifact (ask Legal for clause ID or SOW section).
- [ ] Confirm exact region identifier customer expects (e.g., eu-west-1 vs europe-central).* 
- [ ] Gather telemetry window: sample last 90d routing traces and tokenized latencies (notes: include 10% stratum)
- [ ] Check KMS key location(s) if using customer-managed keys; open KMS ticket if rekey required
- [ ] Review capacity: target region GPUs/edge/proxies can handle expected peak qps + migration bandwidth
- [ ] Determine approach: soft-anchor first or plan hard move with maintenance window
- [ ] Draft customer comms: expected downtime, SLA impact, cost delta, rollback criteria
- [ ] Create evidence bundle template (see Evidence section below)
- [ ] Open a migration-run ticket and link to Confluence design + legal artifact

Soft-anchor run (fast, low-risk):
- 1) Flip routing rule in control-plane to prefer target region for reads; keep writes pinned if policy requires
- 2) Enable prefix/KV cache warmup in target region (bench small warmup for top tenants)
- 3) Start evidence capture for the tenant: attach per-request metadata -> store immutable hash (sha256) and signed timestamp in evidence log
- 4) Monitor latency and error windows for 1–48 hours depending on traffic patterns
- 5) If anomalies, revert routing and document incident
- 6) After 7–30 days of stable soft-anchor, re-evaluate for hard move (if contract requires physical locality)

Hard move run (higher risk):
- 1) Confirm backups + snapshot consistency window; perform test restore in staging region and validate integrity
- 2) Notify customer + schedule low-traffic maintenance window (UTC times, include remediation window)
- 3) Pause writes or switch to write-queueing depending on app semantics (document in ticket)
- 4) Copy storage objects with deterministic object-digests; write transfer manifest with sha256 and object size
- 5) Re-wrap keys if customer-managed KMS requires new key material in target region
- 6) Validate end-to-end with small read/write smoke tests and customer-specified verification prompts
- 7) Promote new storage endpoint, update DNS and control-plane region assertion
- 8) Keep rollback plan and a read-only fallback for at least 24h post-cutover

Evidence bundle (minimum fields):
- tenant_id
- anchor_region_requested (string)
- operator_id (email)
- operator_action_id (ticket id)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- route_snapshot (sha256 digest of routing snapshot file)
- sample_request_logs (list file path or s3:// pointer)
- storage_transfer_manifest (if hard move)
- kms_key_id_origin and kms_key_id_new (if applicable)
- signed_evidence_digest (base64 signature of manifest)

Telemetry checks and quick queries (operator one-liners):
- Query example: "SELECT count(*) FROM routing_logs WHERE tenant=XYZ AND dest_region != 'eu-west-1' AND ts > now()-interval '7 days'"
- Latency drift check: compare p50/p95 pre/post soft-anchor over last 6h
- Evidence completeness: verify each evidence bundle has signed_evidence_digest and manifest size > 0

Risk matrix (summarized):
- Data loss: low if snapshots + verification enforced; medium if streaming writes kept live; high if conversion to new KMS fails
- Downtime: low for soft-anchor; medium-high for hard move depending on write semantics
- Cost delta: estimate storage egress + transfer + dual-region replication during warmup window

Open questions / TODOs (operator notes):
- Q: Do we need to capture per-request bodies for certain regulated customers? Legal to advise on retention duration.
- Q: Can we standardize signed_evidence_digest format (we have 3 variants across teams)? Create RFC.
- TODO: Add automated checklist step in the control-plane UI to stamp operator_action_id and evidence bundle link
- TODO: Run tabletop for read-heavy vs write-heavy customers and capture SLO expectations

Communication templates (brief):
- Customer pre-notice (short): "Planned regional anchoring for tenant <tenant> on <date>. Expected impact: <read latency improvement/ write queueing window>. If you require alternate timing contact SE."
- Internal ops alert: include ticket id, runbook link, rollback criteria, primary engineer, oncall pager

Rollback decision heuristics (quick):
- If error rate > 2x baseline or p95 latency regresses > 300ms for > 5m, trigger immediate rollback
- If storage manifest mismatch > 0.01% of objects, pause and investigate, escalate to SRE and Data Integrity team

Appendix: small operator scripts & snippets (placeholders)
- evidence-digest: sha256sum routing_snapshot.json | base64 -> store as signed_evidence_digest placeholder
- quick-kms-check: aws kms list-keys --region eu-west-1 | grep <tenant_kms_pattern>

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep the evidence bundle lightweight — lawyers hate huge tarballs. Simple signed manifests + sample requests suffice for most audits.
- We should propose a small telemetry label (region_assertion_v1) on every routed request — makes sampling + audits much easier.
- Talk to Legal: define what counts as "residency proof" vs "evidence of routing preference". Very different bar.

References & useful links:
- Confluence: region-assertion-design (linked above)
- Ticket template: ENG-4829
- Ops scripts repo: ops-scripts/pull/214

Last quick revision notes (2025-02-02):
- Added signed_evidence_digest field after discussion with Security (Elena).
- Added explicit rollback latency thresholds.

End of doc.
